Thanks for the intro earlier. Attached is Kestrel's RFI spreadsheet focused on model catalog provenance, open-model licensing, and our requirements for version pinning and update notices. We're particularly focused on:

Samantha —

Thanks for your patience. Please find our consolidated RFI response attached: the completed spreadsheet plus supplemental artifacts (model catalog summary, pinning playbook, and our SOC 2 Type II attestation). A quick summary:
- Provenance: We supply upstream origin links, commit hashes or artifact checksums for catalog models. For a small subset we have upstream attribution only; those entries are footnoted and will be updated on request.
- Licensing: Each model in the catalog includes a license field and an exportable license mapping. We've added conservative legal language where redistribution obligations could apply. For models with restrictive licenses we recommend customer legal review prior to redistribution.
- Pinning & updates: Customers can pin by model-version hash via API or pin on the Console. We provide documented rollback and canary playbooks; we do not automatically pin customer traffic. Customers can request temporary freeze windows via support.

Attachments: Kestrel_RFI_questionnaire_filled.xlsx, Redwood_Model_Catalog_Summary.pdf, SOC2_Type2_Attestation.pdf, pinning-playbook.md

If useful, happy to schedule a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow morning PST to step through the spreadsheet and answer any follow-ups. Please pick a time here: https://calendly.com/redwood/30min
